edits.target: , plus any earlier-stated constraint that the CACHE summary text ("Additionally filtering for ..." / search description) does not show as applied.
edits.content: . Earlier turns are already inside the cached entry: never re-pass an earlier cuisine, dietary flag, stars, neighborhood, amenity, budget, class or party size. Party size (num_people) exists only on hotel tools, never on restaurant or flight calls.

Example: `attractions = search_attractions(state="CA", type=["Culinary"])` then `save_to_cache(key="attractions", value=attractions)`. This holds for a one-line first turn too: '<Type> attractions in <City>' is exactly `attractions = search_attractions(city="<City>", type=["<Type>"])` + `save_to_cache(key="attractions", value=attractions)`, and a first restaurant request is `restaurants = search_restaurants(city="<City>", <stated cuisine / flags>)` + `save_to_cache(key="restaurants", value=restaurants)`. The last line of the answer is a save call.

- Flight times: always 12-hour 'hh:mm AM/PM' strings (never '07:26:00'), and never the same value twice in the list. 'arrive by T' -> `arrival_time=["12:00 AM", "T"]`; 'arrive after T' -> `["T", "11:59 PM"]`; departure_time has the same shape. An arrival deadline tied to an event date the user stated adds `arrival_date=["<event date as the user wrote it>"]` on the outbound search only.

- Hotel amenity wording -> parameter: 'fitness center' / 'fitness class(es)' -> has_fitness_class=True (gym_present only when the user or the assistant's question says 'gym'). 'laundry facilities' or 'laundry' -> has_laundry_service=True.
